observations: Reviewer task ID: none was supplied by the runtime, so task is null.

What I read: I opened storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png, storyboards/page-02.png and review/page-02.png with Read and looked at them. All were readable. I read the full page plan and the first-reading part of the request.

02-1: the caption is top-left and the teal 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' label is top-right. In the art both boxes touch or cover the panel frame corners. That is a frame-edge cosmetic only and the reading order is clear. The over-the-shoulder view of the laptop setup form tells the reader what 'onboarding' means.
02-2: in the art the laptop is in the foreground, so 'here' has a visible referent. This resolves first-reading issue (b). Ananya looks up and to the right, toward the next panel where Meera appears.

02-3: Meera's balloon is read first, then the 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' label at the bottom. The label covers part of Meera's lower body. Framing and size are with the separate artwork review, and the reading is not broken.

02-4: Ananya is left and Meera right, matching 02-2/02-3. The balloon is between them with only a very short stub tail to Ananya. In the art the stub points at Ananya's open mouth, and Meera's mouth is closed. The balloon is clearly closer to Ananya, so the speaker reads correctly. In the placeholder storyboard the balloon only covers Ananya's name label. This was first-reading issue (c), and it is resolved by the actual art, though the tail stays short.
The page ends on the slogan two-shot the source specifies. It works as a quiet close before the time change on page 3.

Without guides: in 02-1 I read the top-left caption, then the top-right label. In the middle row, Ananya's line is left, then Meera's line and the Care label on the right. In the bottom panel, 'One team. Better coordination.' is read last.
No non-consecutive balloons are close to each other. The labels are visually different (teal boxes), so they do not read as speech.

transitions.observation: Morning reception changes to an evening office. A sunset window, the laptop setup form and the caption mark it as a later, separate time. Ananya's coat and bun carry her identity across.
Same office, same evening window. We move from over the shoulder to a front view. Her hand goes from the keyboard to the trackpad and her chin, and the laptop is still open.

Ananya's upward gaze to the right leads into Meera standing in the office with the staff phone. The open laptop behind her on the desk shows it is the same room. 'And our team' continues Ananya's sentence.
Two-shot of the same office. Meera, still holding the phone, stands right of the seated Ananya. The left-right placement agrees with 02-2/02-3.

The evening office changes to bright daylight at a reception desk with a monitor, where a new man walks in waving. The light, the new tidy desk and the stranger signal a later day without a caption, as in the source. 'I'd like to see the doctor' makes him a patient.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading had the same order. Issue (b), 'here' without a referent, is resolved by the laptop in the art. Issue (c), the speaker of the short 02-4 tail, is resolved by the art: Ananya's mouth is open, Meera's is closed, and the balloon is next to Ananya. Issue (d), boxes on the frame edge, is cosmetic. Issue (a), the abrupt jump to onboarding, and issue (e), the slogan ending, follow the source structure and the caption carries them. I do not treat them as storyboard failures.
